transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-11-12
Start: 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Rafael (Redwood Security), Laura (Acme Head of Security), Mark (Acme Platform), Nina (Acme IT Ops)

Summary:
High-level security review focused on SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning and RBAC least-privilege model. Discussed SAML IdP/ SP setup, SCIM attribute mappings, group sync cadence, role design for least privilege, audit logging retention, KMS integration for envelope encryption, and SOC2/ISO evidence paths. Agreed next steps to share configuration guides, SCIM samples, and schedule an RBAC walkthrough.

Topics:
- SSO/SAML setup and metadata exchange
- SCIM provisioning and attribute/group mapping
- RBAC models and least-privilege role templates
- Audit logs, retention, and export for SIEM
- Encryption key management (KMS/HSM) and bring-your-own-key
- Data residency concerns and SOC2/ISO artifacts

Transcript:
00:00:03 - Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to make sure we covered the SSO, SCIM and RBAC flow end-to-end today. Quick roll call?
00:00:12 - Laura: Hi, Laura here from Acme security - happy to be here.
00:00:16 - Mark: Mark from Platform.
00:00:18 - Nina: Nina from IT Ops.
00:00:21 - Samira: Samira, Redwood SE, and Rafael from our security team is on too.
00:00:27 - Rafael: Hey all, quick note, I might drop a couple of times but I'll be on for the core review.

00:01:05 - Jordan: Cool. So first question, are you already using an IdP like Okta or Auth0? and what's the current SCIM provisioning story?
00:01:14 - Laura: We're on Okta for SSO and we have a pretty aggressive provisioning cadence right now. We use Okta's SCIM connector to push users and groups to a couple internal apps. We don't have a connector for Redwood yet, so we're looking for best practices.
00:01:28 - Samira: Great, we have a Redwood SAML SP metadata blob we can share; our SCIM supports Okta out-of-the-box, we also support group push. We typically map Okta groups to RBAC roles, but we wanted to review your least-privilege model first.
00:01:43 - Mark: One of our constraints is group explosion — we have hundreds of Okta groups. We want to avoid syncing everything. So we need filtering and mapping guidance.
00:01:58 - Rafael: Also to note, Acme is SOC2 type II and in process for ISO 27001 recert; we need to demonstrate how audit logs and provisioning events are captured. How granular are your logs?
00:02:12 - Jordan: Our audit logs capture auth events, SCIM provisioning events, API key creation/rotation, role assignment changes, and admin console actions. We have a 12-month default retention for audit events in hosted plans, and longer retention options for enterprise. We can export logs to S3 or a SIEM via streaming.
00:02:29 - Nina: Can you show an example? Are the logs immutable and signed?
00:02:34 - Samira: The logs are append-only in the control plane; for enterprise we support write-once policies and can stream to your log bucket. We don't currently provide cryptographic signing per event but we do support S3 access controls + object lock depending on plan; we can discuss HSM-backed attestation for higher tier private deployments.

00:03:10 - Laura: Ok, on SSO specifics: we need SAML attributes to include email, name, employee id, and groups. We also want the SAML audience and ACS URL to be explicit.
00:03:22 - Samira: Yes we require Email (NameID) plus an optional groups attribute for group-based role mapping. We'll send SP metadata (entityID, ACS URL, cert) after the call. We support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows.
00:03:36 - Mark: About SCIM, can we filter group sync to by-prefix? e.g., only sync groups prefixed with redwood- or prod-?
00:03:44 - Samira: Yes — we support filter expressions on the connector side and can apply server-side mapping rules so you don't sync everything. We'll send a sample SCIM mapping config.

00:04:12 - Speaker 1: [inaudible] question on deprovisioning — how immediate is user removal?
00:04:18 - Rafael: That's crucial. We need ensure offboarding is timely to meet our compliance window.
00:04:23 - Samira: By default SCIM push for user deactivation is immediate; if you do full delete we'll follow the SCIM delete request. We also optionally support a disabled state in Redwood for soft-deprovision where tokens are invalidated and data is retained per your retention setting.
00:04:37 - Laura: That soft-deprovision state is helpful for audit, but we also want a guaranteed repeatable process to revoke keys and sessions. How do you handle token/session revocation?
00:04:47 - Jordan: We revoke API keys immediately via control plane and we have a session invalidation endpoint. For long-lived model access tokens used by agents you can rotate keys and we surface usage per token so you can detect anomalies.

00:05:20 - Mark: On RBAC, we want least-privilege templates to start from — e.g., Viewer, Editor, Admin, Owner and then environment-specific bindings. Does Redwood support resource-scoped roles?
00:05:33 - Samira: Yes, resource-scoped roles are supported. You can bind roles at org, project, model, or route level. We recommend starting with a minimal set for production: read-only, inference-only (no model upload), model-management (upload/rollout), and admin (billing + settings). We'll share role templates.
00:05:51 - Laura: And SCIM group->role mapping — is that one-to-many? If a user is in multiple groups which map to multiple roles, how is precedence handled?
00:06:01 - Samira: We have a deterministic precedence policy: most restrictive wins for effective permissions unless you explicitly create a composite role. We'll include that precedence doc in the mapping guide.

00:06:40 - Nina: Encryption — we need BYOK, KMS integration. We manage keys in AWS KMS and HSM for certain workloads. Can Redwood support customer-managed keys?
00:06:51 - Rafael: And we need to know which data is encrypted at rest vs in transit, and where the envelope keys are stored.
00:06:57 - Jordan: For Hosted we support Bring-Your-Own-Key via AWS KMS for enterprise plans, where you supply a key ARN. Data at rest is encrypted with envelope encryption; the data keys are encrypted with your KMS key in the control plane. In Private deployments you can bring HSM integration and control the KMS entirely. All in-transit is TLS 1.2+ with strong ciphers.
00:07:18 - Mark: Are model weights or logs ever decrypted in plaintext in any shared environment?
00:07:23 - Rafael: We need clarity for audit.
00:07:26 - Samira: Model weights are stored encrypted; transient CPU/GPU memory may hold plaintext during inference but never written to persistent storage unencrypted. For hosted shared infra we enforce tenant isolation, for dedicated/private you get isolated GPUs and storage. We'll include an architecture diagram in the security pack.

00:08:10 - Laura: Data residency — some PII work must stay in EU. Can we restrict processing regionally?
00:08:17 - Jordan: Yes, we support region pinning for requests and data. For Hosted customers you can choose EU region endpoints; for Dedicated we can provision capacity in your region, and for Private it's on-prem. We'll document the data flow and where logs/keys live.

00:08:50 - Speaker 2: Quick question on evidence for SOC2 — what artifacts can we get for vendor assessment?
00:08:56 - Rafael: Also need ISO evidence buckets.
00:09:00 - Samira: We can provide SOC2 Type II report under NDA, System Description, encryption diagrams, access control policies, RBAC configs, and audit log exports. For ISO, we share applicable controls mapping, and we can provide change logs and evidence exports for specific periods.

00:09:34 - Laura: For RBAC review, can we walk through a sample of role assignment and an admin action that changes permissions so we can see the audit trail?
00:09:44 - Samira: Absolutely, that's part of the RBAC walkthrough action item. Rafael will prep a demo that shows role grant, token rotation, and the corresponding audit entries.

00:10:12 - Jordan: A common ask is just-in-time admin; do you have a workflow for temporary elevation?
00:10:20 - Samira: We have an API to grant time-limited roles and integrated expiring bindings. Right now you need to script it with the API or use our automation hooks; we're piloting an approval workflow in console for enterprise.

00:10:45 - Mark: On SCIM attributes, we want custom attributes like 'cost-center' and 'manager' — does the Redwood SCIM endpoint accept custom attrs?
00:10:55 - Samira: We accept custom attributes with a namespaced extension. We'll send an example payload. Be aware that custom attributes are stored as metadata and can be used in policy conditions but may not be indexed for fast queries.

00:11:30 - Speaker 1: Any rate limits on SCIM calls? We have batch provisioning during onboarding which is heavy.
00:11:37 - Samira: For hosted, we have throttling by default; for enterprise we raise limits or accept a bulk CSV import via secure upload. We'll coordinate a one-time import plan if you need it.

00:12:05 - Nina: About SAML certificate rotation — what's the recommended cadence and can we do double-cert to avoid downtime?
00:12:13 - Samira: Yes support for certificate rollover: you can provision the new cert and we support overlapping validity windows. We'll provide steps in the SAML guide.

00:12:40 - Jordan: Let's talk about privilege escalation monitoring — do you expose alerts for unusual role grants or abnormal admin activity?
00:12:48 - Rafael: We need to plug into our SIEM for alerting.
00:12:52 - Samira: We emit admin events and role-change events that you can stream via our event export to Kinesis/SQS/S3 or syslog to your SIEM. We can also send webhook alerts for certain event types. We'll include event schema.

00:13:30 - Laura: For least-privilege mapping, we want suggested templates tied to product paths: e.g., inference-only role must have no model upload, no billing, limited read access to logs.
00:13:42 - Samira: We'll share template JSON for roles and an example of policy bindings referencing route-level resources.

00:14:10 - Mark: One more on SCIM: how do you handle group renames vs group deletes? We had issues where rename created orphans in other systems.
00:14:20 - Samira: We match groups by immutable id if provided by Okta, otherwise by displayName. We recommend you enable group immutable IDs in Okta. If rename occurs and immutable ID matches, we update displayName; if no immutable ID we treat as delete + create. We'll document best practices.

00:14:55 - Speaker 3: Question about delegation and sub-orgs — can we have nested orgs and delegation so business units administer their own projects?
00:15:03 - Samira: Yes, Redwood supports org -> workspace -> project scoping and you can delegate admin roles at workspace level. We'll include that topology in the RBAC doc.

00:15:40 - Jordan: Anything else regarding legal or procurement?
00:15:44 - Laura: We do need to run the DPA and security questionnaires; please share those.
00:15:49 - Jordan: We'll send the DPA and our security questionnaire pack after this; Samira will attach the SAML/SCIM guides and Rafael will attach the RBAC templates.

00:16:15 - Mark: In terms of timeline we want to pilot next month — two weeks to configure SSO + SCIM and then RBAC test. Is that realistic?
00:16:25 - Samira: Yes, for a scoped pilot it's realistic: share group list and a test org, we can do initial setup in 1-2 days and then iterate. We'll also capture benchmarks for audit events and provisioning time.

00:16:50 - Laura: For audit evidence, can we get a sample of the event schema so our auditors can parse it?
00:16:55 - Rafael: And can we get examples of API key rotation events?
00:16:58 - Samira: Yes — event schema with examples will be included.

00:17:20 - Jordan: Quick note on infrastructure isolation: for Dedicated we provide dedicated GPU pools and network isolation. For Private, full control. For hosted multi-tenant we provide strong logical isolation plus audit controls; we'll clarify this in the pack.

00:17:45 - Mark: Any FIPS or special crypto compliance?
00:17:49 - Samira: We use industry standard ciphers and can support FIPS-enabled HSMs in Private deployments; for hosted we can discuss options depending on contract.

00:18:15 - Nina: For user lifecycle, is there a way to do periodic entitlement reviews?
00:18:21 - Samira: We support exports for entitlement reports and can automate a monthly review via the API.

00:18:40 - Laura: Great. Let's recap next steps.
00:18:44 - Jordan: Recap: Redwood to share SAML SP metadata, SCIM mapping example, role templates, audit event schema, SOC2 and ISO artifacts (under NDA). Acme to provide group list and pilot org and timeline. We'll schedule a 30-minute RBAC walkthrough next week.
00:19:03 - Mark: Sounds good.
00:19:06 - Nina: Thanks everyone.
00:19:08 - Rafael: I'll put together the RBAC demo and the role precedence notes.
00:19:15 - Jordan: Perfect, we'll follow up via email and put items in the CRM. Thanks all.

End of transcript.
